1. **Header** — title text style (weight/size/line-height/letter-spacing/colour), the See-Full-History link's exact text style/colour/hover-if-visible, padding (re-verify per above), alignment.

4. **Cross-page consistency** — does the Rail look identical embedded in PDP vs PLP, or does either page apply its own wrapper spacing/width constraint that changes how the rail actually renders there? - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx` + `.css.ts` (just-fixed header, see above)
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — the `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row (image-only, no name/price/bag — confirm the real page nodes still show this, i.e. no design drift toward showing more)
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` — the container, and its actual mount points: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (PDP) and `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (PLP, lines ~789-792) — check what layout props each passes.

Structured, most-severe/most-confident first. CONFIRMED (certain, values directly conflict) vs. PLAUSIBLE (looks wrong, couldn't fully verify — say why) vs. Could-not-verify (rate-limited, dead node, ambiguous breakpoint mapping). For each finding: exact Figma node + value, exact file:line + current value, concrete visual consequence. Explicitly state whether the two already-fixed header commits hold up against this fuller page-context check or need revisiting. Do not fix anything — audit only. Keep the report tight — bullets, not prose essays per finding.

**Directive:** Re-audit the Recently Viewed Rail exhaustively using real PDP/PLP page nodes (not individually-copied links), re-verify the already-fixed header padding against page-embedded context, and check cross-page consistency.

## CONFIRMED — most important finding, changes the whole picture

**PLP's Figma "Recently Viewed" instance is a stale, structurally different placeholder — not a real disagreement with the code.** Checked all three breakpoints on both pages via `get_metadata` on the actual "Recently Viewed" instance node inside each page frame:

- **PDP** (Desktop `7998:13508`, Tablet `8028:85559`, Mobile `8272:28947`) — all three are real instances of the confirmed Rail component: children literally named `title-and-link` + `group`/`Product-card`, referencing the exact same `40000307:*` / `40000538:*` / `40000730:*` node family already used as this build's authoritative Rail source. Desktop 1440×528, Tablet 768×437.85, Mobile 402×355.82 — all match exactly what's already built.
- **PLP** (Desktop `2257:7938`, Tablet `3041:21409`, Mobile `3601:80788`) — all three reference a **completely different component**, named "Recently Viewed Product" (not "Product-card"), IDs in the `2257:*`/`2832:*` family — **with no header/see-full-history-link instance at all, at any breakpoint.** Dimensions also differ: Desktop 1440×396 (not 528 — no header, shorter cards), Tablet's own page frame is 1024px wide (not 768, like PDP's), Mobile 402×272 (not 355.82).

This is not a real spec conflict to resolve by changing code — it means PLP's specific page-composition frame in this Figma file predates the final Rail component and was never updated, while PDP's was. The current codebase already renders the identical `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` on both pages, matching PDP's correctly-updated reference. Recommend flagging this to whoever owns the Figma file for cleanup, not treating it as an implementation gap.

**Already-fixed header padding (commit `0809687`) holds up — re-verification found nothing new.** PDP's page-embedded instances reference the exact same component node IDs already checked in the prior audit (`40000538:20306` Desktop, `40000730:13364` Tablet, `40000538:25031` Mobile) — same component, same values, nothing to revisit.

## Could not verify / not attempted this pass

- **No fresh exhaustive atom-level style extraction** (exact text styles, colours, card internals) of the confirmed PDP-side component — it's the identical component already covered in the prior audit pass; budget went to the cross-page-consistency question instead, which surfaced the bigger finding above.
- **No screenshot taken** to visually confirm "PLP has no header" — the structural metadata (different component family, zero header child across all 3 breakpoints) is unambiguous enough to report as CONFIRMED, but a screenshot would be a cheap final sanity check if wanted.
- **PDP-vs-PLP wrapper `mx` prop consistency** (`recommended-products/index.tsx`'s bleed handling) — not freshly re-checked this pass; relying on an already-read comment in `product-list/index.tsx` (from earlier in this build) stating its own `mx` value matches PDP's reasoning, not Cart's.
